briefs.explicit:
MISSION BRIEF S-015
Units: metres, seconds, kilograms. Time starts at t = 0 when every robot leaves its start location.

Locations (x, y, zone):
- base: (0, 0), outdoor
- office roof: (-34, -27), roof
- electrical room: (149, 63), indoor
- gate 2: (46, 112), outdoor
- site B: (66, -34), outdoor

Robots:
- M1 (mobile_manipulator): starts at base. Drives on the road grid (travel distance = |dx| + |dy|) at 1.5 m/s; can reach outdoor and indoor locations, not roofs. Equipment: cargo carrier (max 7 kg), robotic arm, camera. Endurance: 3180 s, including the return to its start.
- M2 (mobile_manipulator): starts at base. Drives on the road grid (travel distance = |dx| + |dy|) at 1.5 m/s; can reach outdoor and indoor locations, not roofs. Equipment: cargo carrier (max 5 kg), robotic arm, camera. Endurance: 3420 s, including the return to its start.
- D1 (quadcopter): starts at base. Flies in straight lines at 8 m/s; can reach outdoor and roof locations, not indoor ones. Equipment: camera, cargo carrier (max 2 kg). Endurance: 900 s, including the return to its start.

Tasks:
- T1: Inspect office roof with a camera. Location: office roof. Duration: 120 s. Needs: camera. Deadline: finished by t = 240 s.
- T2: Deliver the battery pack (4 kg) to gate 2. Location: gate 2. Duration: 30 s. Needs: cargo carrier (payload 4 kg). Deadline: finished by t = 300 s.
- T3: Deliver the toolkit (6 kg) to site B. Location: site B. Duration: 60 s. Needs: cargo carrier (payload 6 kg).
- T4: Deliver the cable reel (7 kg) to site B. Location: site B. Duration: 60 s. Needs: cargo carrier (payload 7 kg).
- T5: Deliver the spare pump (6 kg) to electrical room. Location: electrical room. Duration: 30 s. Needs: cargo carrier (payload 6 kg).

Rules:
1. Every task is done by exactly one robot. A robot does its tasks one at a time, in the order you list them, travelling between task locations.
2. A robot can only do a task if it has the needed equipment, enough payload capacity, and can reach the task location.
3. A task that must start after another task waits until that task is finished, even if a different robot does it.
4. Each robot must be back at its start location before its endurance runs out.
5. Every task must be finished by t = 900 s.

Objective: minimise the finish time of the last task (the makespan).
briefs.informal:
Here's what we need from the robots today.

Positions are in metres from the base at (0, 0). Drones fly straight and can't go indoors; ground robots follow the road grid (so they travel |dx| + |dy|) and can't get onto roofs. Everyone leaves their start spot at time zero.

Places: office roof (-34, -27, a rooftop); electrical room (149, 63, indoors); gate 2 (46, 112, outside); site B (66, -34, outside).

The fleet: M1 is our mobile manipulator at base: gripper arm, camera, room for 7 kg, moves at 1.5 m/s and lasts 53 minutes including getting back. M2 is our mobile manipulator at base: gripper arm, camera, room for 5 kg, moves at 1.5 m/s and lasts 57 minutes including getting back. D1, a quadcopter waiting at base, carries a camera, cruises at 8 m/s, lifts up to 2 kg and has 15 minutes of flight time, return trip included.

Jobs:
(T1) Get eyes on office roof and check the panels - that takes 2 minutes on site and it has to be finished within the first 4 minutes.
(T2) Get the battery pack (4 kg) over to gate 2 - that takes 0.5 minutes on site and it has to be finished within the first 5 minutes.
(T3) Get the toolkit (6 kg) over to site B - that takes 1 minute on site.
(T4) Drop the cable reel off at site B; it weighs 7 kg - that takes 1 minute on site.
(T5) Get the spare pump (6 kg) over to electrical room - that takes 0.5 minutes on site.

Everything has to be wrapped up within 15 minutes of the start, and the sooner the last job finishes, the better. Every robot has to make it back to where it started before its battery runs out.
